narrative.northStar: An instrument that never lies, and never shouts.
narrative.overview: Hutch is a local-first multi-bot agent workspace: a conversation-first console where a person sends tasks to bots, watches real execution, and decides consequential approvals. The design job is trust under time pressure — every pixel either helps someone understand what the machine is actually doing, or it is chrome that should shrink. Layered graphite surfaces carry elevation by shadow and hairline rather than glow; colour does jobs (emerald brand, azure interaction, amber person-needed, rose failure); the 3D mascot appears only in first-run moments while per-bot identity stays a lightweight sigil.
keyCharacteristics: Layered graphite surfaces with elevation by offset+blur shadow and a top hairline — never glow.
One conversation column (760px) carries the story; operational ledgers support it as tables.
Colour does jobs: emerald brand, azure interaction, amber person-needed-now, rose failure — everything else neutral.
Mono type reserved for machine-measured values with tabular numerals.
Motion is short, state-linked and disable-able; the typing dots are the one live animation.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text caps at ~72ch; anything wider is layout debt.

rules.name: The One-Ink Rule
rules.body: Emerald fills always carry near-black ink (#04140d); white on emerald is forbidden (≈2.5:1).

rules.name: The Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where a person must act now — pending approvals, deadlines under two minutes, the attention badge. Never as decoration, never on done or failed.

rules.name: The Scale Rule
rules.body: Every corner radius comes from rounded.*; no ad-hoc values.

rules.name: The Measured Rule
rules.body: Mono type is only for values the server measured — never prose, labels, or marketing.

dos: Do take every radius from rounded.*; keep the pill only for chips.
Do pair every icon with a word for state; give every control a visible focus ring.
Do use mono only for machine-measured values.
Do show real server state: if the API cannot confirm it, say "unknown".
Do keep motion short, functional and state-linked; honour reduced motion and the Reduce effects override.
donts: Never put white on emerald, or amber on something that isn't person-needed.
Never box tool calls, or wrap decided approvals in cards.
Never run ambient loops, pulsing dots on idle state, or animated backgrounds behind work.
Never show a count, status or receipt the server did not produce.
Never add a radius outside the scale, or a colour outside the palette.
